sections.h2: Which county bills property tax for St. Paul?
sections.html:
Ramsey County bills and collects St. Paul property tax, and the Ramsey County Assessor sets the value. St. Paul is the state capital, incorporated on March 4, 1854, with 51.97 square miles of land and 4.13 of water along the Mississippi River. Census QuickFacts counts 306,684 residents in July 2025, a drop of 1.5% from the April 2020 base.

The county offices you will deal with sit in the Plato Building at 90 Plato Blvd. West, Saint Paul, MN 55107, and they answer Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Here is who answers what:

  • Property Tax Services: 651-266-2222, for payments, statements and penalties
  • County Assessor: 651-266-2131, for value and classification questions
  • Homestead Unit: 651-266-2040, for homestead applications
  • Delinquent tax line: 651-266-2002
  • Recorder's Office: 651-266-2050, for recorded deeds and other real estate documents

sections.h2: What do St. Paul housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
St. Paul is a city of renters and owners in nearly equal measure. Census QuickFacts reports a 52.9% owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024, with 125,249 households and 2.37 people per household.

  • Median owner-occupied home value of $294,500
  • Median gross rent of $1,281, and median owner costs of $1,911 with a mortgage
  • Median household income of $73,394, with 43.8% of adults holding a bachelor's degree or higher
  • A mean commute of 21.1 minutes, and 83.7% living in the same house a year earlier
  • 5,994 people per square mile of land in 2020

A seller's bill depends on how the parcel is classified. Ramsey County publishes separate tax calculators for homestead versus non-homestead houses, duplex-triplex properties and apartments with four or more units.

sections.h2: When is St. Paul property tax due?
sections.html:
Real property tax is paid in two installments, May 15 and October 15, and a weekend due date moves to the next business day. Escrow customers do not need to act, since the mortgage company pays. Tax of $100 or less on real property must be paid in full with the first installment.

Ramsey County property tax calendar for St. Paul parcels (county Pay Property Tax page)
TypeFirst installmentSecond installment
Real propertyMay 15October 15
AgriculturalMay 15October 15
Leased government-owned personal propertyMay 15October 15
Other personal propertyMay 15, total dueNone
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

The county mails two notices a year per property. In mid-March you get the tax statement and a value notice, the latter used to set next year's tax. In November comes the proposed tax notice, with proposed amounts for the following year and meeting dates for levy and budget hearings. Homeowners can choose electronic delivery through eNoticesOnline.

sections.h2: What late penalties apply in Ramsey County?
sections.html:
Penalty starts the day after a due date and grows each month, and late payments are applied to penalty first, then to tax. The county's 2026 schedule has separate rates for homesteads and cabins versus non-homesteads. A homestead first half unpaid after May 15 costs 2% on May 16, 4% on June 1, 5% on July 1 and 8% by October 1, rising to 10% on January 2, 2027. A non-homestead first half runs 4%, 8%, 9%, 12% and then 14% at those same points.

For a second half, a homestead starts at 2% on October 16 and reaches 7% on January 2, while a non-homestead starts at 4% and reaches 11%. If both halves are unpaid, the combined rate begins at 5% for a homestead and 8% for a non-homestead on October 16.

Two relief options exist:

  • One-time waiver: one penalty waiver per parcel every 10 years, for either the first or the second half. Requests with payment must arrive between May 16 and October 15 for a first half, and between October 16 and December 20 for a second half. A waiver is denied if the original payment bounced, if the parcel has delinquent tax or a confession of judgment, or if the waiver was used in the last 10 years.
  • Hardship abatement: a request to the County Auditor/Treasurer, generally granted only for exceptional hardship such as hospitalization. Call 651-266-2222.

A returned payment carries a $30 fee, and partial payments are accepted.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a St. Paul property value?
sections.html:
Call the Ramsey County Assessor at 651-266-2131 first. The county says many issues are resolved by phone, but you will not speak with an appraiser right away: you give your concern, and an appraiser calls back within three days. A recent appraisal or a sale of your property, sent by mail or electronically, supports a claim of overvaluation or wrong classification.

On-site inspections follow state law, which calls for a physical review of each property at least once every five years. Appraisers visit nearly 32,000 Ramsey County properties a year, and the county sends no notice before a visit. An interactive map on the county website shows when your area is scheduled in the current cycle.

Homestead status changes the bill, and the county's Homestead page has the details for sellers and buyers:

  • The state homestead market value exclusion lowers the taxable value only for properties valued under $517,200.
  • Homestead is also one qualifying factor for the state Property Tax Refund.
  • The last day to own and occupy for the current assessment year, and to apply for residential or agricultural homestead, is December 31, so a buyer closing before then should apply.
  • Filers may now use an ITIN in place of a Social Security number.

sections.h2: What happens if St. Paul property tax goes delinquent?
sections.html:
Tax is delinquent on January 1 of the year after it was due. The penalty rate rises then, and interest runs on the unpaid tax, penalty and fees at 10% a year, increasing monthly. A $25 delinquent fee covers publication and notice.

Owners have three years to pay everything and redeem the property, and payment plans called Confessions of Judgment are available. If the redemption period ends unpaid, forfeiture begins, and the county gives formal notice in several ways:

  • A courtesy letter in the first week of April
  • A list of affected parcels printed in the county's newspaper for two weeks in May
  • Copies posted at the Property Records and Property Tax Services offices
  • Service by the sheriff on an occupant, or a posted notice for vacant and land-only property
  • A certified letter in June

Payments go to penalties first, then interest, fees and tax. The delinquent tax line at 651-266-2002 can confirm whether a parcel on the published list has since been paid.

sections.h2: How should a St. Paul seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Get a current figure from Property Tax Services at 651-266-2222 before the closing date, since the first half may be paid while the second half is still open, or both may be unpaid. Ask for the parcel's penalty status as well, because the schedule changes on specific dates such as June 1, July 1 and October 16.

Recorded documents go through the Recorder's Office, which keeps official real estate records for the county and notes that it does not help complete legal forms. Once a document is recorded it is permanent and cannot be removed or altered, so have a title company or attorney review the deed first.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in St. Paul, Minnesota?
faqs.a: Ramsey County Property Tax Services does, at 90 Plato Blvd. West in Saint Paul. The phone is 651-266-2222, and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What are the St. Paul property tax due dates?
faqs.a: May 15 and October 15 for real property, with a weekend date moving to the next business day. Manufactured homes are due August 31 and November 15.

faqs.q: Can Ramsey County waive a late property tax penalty?
faqs.a: Yes, once per parcel every 10 years, for either the first or second half. Send the signed waiver form with your payment, postmarked or dropped off by the deadline in the county's schedule.

faqs.q: How do I question my St. Paul property value?
faqs.a: Call the County Assessor at 651-266-2131. An appraiser returns the call within three days, and a recent appraisal or sale of the property can be sent as support.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem delinquent St. Paul property tax?
faqs.a: Three years to pay all delinquent tax and redeem the property, with payment plans available. Call 651-266-2002 for the current balance and interest.
